reason: Prior panel32 calls passed correctness but showed mixed paired results in both battery modes, with no promotion. A one-entry helper loop is a distinct, source-expressible test of the same work with fewer SME transitions; its assembly, pointer, and scratch-lifetime risks are high, so require the byte-identical helper check and full validation. The first three proposals describe substantially the same change and should be treated as duplicates, not separate experiments. The three K-loop proposals also converge on a 256-iteration two-K body; test at most one. The historical two-step loop did not promote, so this narrower loop-control change has lower expected benefit. Scratch reuse and B-panel packing need broad assembly/layout changes; transpose fusion is high risk, and full-shape transpose needs an unavailable generated helper. No supplied score shows a candidate above 1800 GFLOP/s or proves a performance cause.
